reviewBoundary: Four newly written complete cloze narratives for junior learners, not sentence substitutions in an old passage. Each gap has an explicit contextual key and a rationale covering every distractor. Same-author review and schema/grading checks only; no independent learner calibration.

units.title: 完形填空 · 空碗的重量

materials.title: The empty bowl
materials.text:
I wanted to bake a cake for Dad's birthday. My grandmother agreed to help, but she said I should do the measuring myself. I put a large bowl on the kitchen scales and began to add flour.

The recipe said 200 grams. When the number reached 200, I ____1____ pouring. There was surprisingly little flour in the bowl. 'This cake will be very ____2____,' I said.

Grandma did not add more flour immediately. She asked me to take the bowl ____3____ the scales. Then she put the empty bowl back. The number was 160.

'I counted the weight of the bowl as well!' I said. Grandma ____4____. She showed me a button that made the number return to zero while the empty bowl was still on the scales. Now the scales would show only the weight of what I ____5____.

We started again. This time I checked the number before and after putting in each ingredient. I also wrote a short ____6____ beside the recipe: 'Put bowl on scales, then press zero.' I wanted to remember the right order next time.

The cake came out well. Dad asked whether I had made it all by ____7____. 'Mostly,' I said, 'but Grandma helped me understand a mistake.'

Later, I used a different bowl to weigh some apples. It was much lighter than the first one. I knew that simply taking 160 away from every reading would not ____8____. Each bowl had its own weight.

Before I put in the apples, I checked that the display showed ____9____. Baking had taught me that a useful number depends on knowing exactly what you are ____10____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Reaching the target makes the narrator stop pouring. Enjoyed describes a feeling rather than the boundary action; forgot does not fit the intentional response to the number.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Surprisingly little flour suggests a small cake. No price comparison supports expensive, and no delay supports late.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Take the bowl off the scales removes it so the empty bowl can be put back. Through and towards do not describe removal from the weighing surface.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Grandma confirms the discovery and demonstrates zeroing, so agreed. She remains present, ruling out disappeared, and no complaint is described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Zeroing leaves the weight of newly added ingredients. Remembered is not a physical load and washed does not express putting ingredients into the bowl.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The quoted procedural reminder is a note. It is neither a humorous joke nor a narrative story.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The narrator reports whether I had made it by myself. Herself would refer to a female third person and himself to a male third person, not I.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Subtracting the old bowl's weight cannot work for every different bowl. Wait and hurt do not describe whether this calculation is effective.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The empty new bowl must be zeroed before adding apples. 160 belonged to the old bowl and 200 to the flour target, so neither is the initial display wanted.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The story concerns identifying what a weight measures. No sale or concealment supports selling or hiding.

units.title: 完形填空 · 明信片上的折痕

materials.title: The folded postcard
materials.text:
During a holiday, Leo bought a postcard showing a mountain village. He planned to send it to his cousin, but first he wanted to find the place where the photograph had been taken.

'It must be near the square,' he said. The church was in the middle of the picture, with a narrow street on its ____1____ side. Leo walked along the street to the right of the church, but the view looked wrong. The church appeared much ____2____ than it did on the card.

He went farther away. Now its size looked right, but a tall building stood in front of it. Leo was ready to ____3____ when a shopkeeper noticed the postcard in his hand.

'May I see the whole card?' she asked. Leo unfolded it. He had bent one edge back so it would fit into his pocket. A small bridge had been ____4____ by the fold.

'That bridge is across the river,' the shopkeeper said. 'The photograph was taken from the path on the other ____5____.'

Leo crossed the bridge and followed the riverside path. At one point he stopped and held up the card. The church, street and bridge were all in the ____6____ places. He had found the view.

He took his own photograph, then sat down to write to his cousin. He described not only the village but also his ____7____ in finding the spot.

Before posting the card, he carefully made it ____8____ again. 'You need the whole picture,' he wrote at the end.

When his cousin replied, she said the story was more interesting than a list of sights. Leo had spent an hour looking for one place, but the postcard now held a ____9____ of his own. Next time he used a picture as a guide, he would check that no part of it was ____10____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The next sentence explicitly says Leo follows the street to the right. Left contradicts that cue and upper does not match the lateral direction used.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Moving farther away then makes its size look right, showing it initially appeared larger. Quieter concerns sound, and older concerns age, neither solved by distance in the stated way.

questions.prompt: Choose the best phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Repeated failed views make Leo ready to give up. Nothing suggests sleep for wake up or a debt for pay back.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Folding the edge hides the printed bridge. The fold neither builds a real bridge nor crosses it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 5.
questions.explanation: He must cross the river to the other side. Floor concerns a building and page a document, not the opposite riverbank.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Finding the view means the landmarks align in the same places as on the card. Wrong denies the match, and empty cannot describe places already occupied by those landmarks.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The search involved difficulty finding the spot. There was no promise made about the search and no prize awarded.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Unfolding and smoothing the card makes it flat. Wet and dark have no role in restoring the folded image before posting.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 9.
questions.explanation: His personal search gives the postcard a memory of his own. The passage values a story rather than a price or the postal address.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The hidden bridge caused the error, so he checks that no part is missing from view. Popularity and colour do not address an incomplete guiding image.

units.title: 完形填空 · 两个下午的电影

materials.title: Two afternoons in one film
materials.text:
Our class was making a film about a girl who missed a bus. We filmed her leaving school on Monday and running towards the bus stop on Wednesday.

When we watched both parts together, everyone laughed. At school, our actor carried a red umbrella. In the street, her hands were ____1____. We had forgotten the umbrella on Wednesday.

"Perhaps viewers will not notice," someone said. But the umbrella covered half her face in the first shot. It was hard to ____2____.

We could film the street scene again, but our actor had returned her borrowed uniform. Finding the same clothes and gathering everyone would take another week. We needed another ____3____.

Our teacher asked what could happen between the scenes. In the last school image, a friend stood beside the door, with her face outside the picture. "She could ____4____ the umbrella to that friend," I suggested.

We filmed just two hands and the umbrella. No uniforms were needed. Our actor's voice saying "Please keep this for me" explained the ____5____. We inserted the shot between the original scenes.

Now the umbrella did not simply ____6____. Its absence had a reason. The girl wanted her hands free to run.

Afterwards, someone kept a list of what each actor wore and ____7____. We had learned to check objects as well as lines. A film need not show every second, but its parts must ____8____.

At the screening, viewers followed the story easily. They did not need to know that the extra shot came from a third day. They needed a ____9____ story, and those few seconds had helped us ____10____ one.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The forgotten umbrella means she carries nothing: empty hands. Cold and dirty concern conditions not mentioned; heavy contradicts absence of an object.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The bright umbrella in front of her face is hard for viewers to ignore. Borrow, open and repair concern handling the umbrella, not noticing continuity.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 3.
questions.explanation: They need an alternative solution to reshooting. A uniform is one missing resource, not the desired overall approach; audience and street do not address the continuity problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Passing the umbrella to a friend explains free hands and is shown by the added hands-only shot. Compare and describe leave it with her; sell has no support in the friendly request to keep it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The spoken request explains the filmed action of handing it over. Weather is not discussed, production delay is not part of the story, and uniforms are deliberately outside the new shot.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 6.
questions.explanation: The new shot gives a reason for the umbrella's disappearance from the next scene. Shine, break and grow are not the unexplained change between the original shots.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The list tracks clothing and carried objects for continuity. Believed, heard and promised describe mental or verbal content rather than the visible object problem.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Omitted seconds are acceptable if shown parts connect coherently. Compete and wait do not express continuity; repeat would require unnecessary duplication rather than connection.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Following without confusion requires a clear story. Secret is contrary to communicating it; longer is not the goal; silent contradicts the explanatory spoken line.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The added shot helps create a clear story. Cancel and forget undo the task; measure has no appropriate story-production meaning here.

units.title: 完形填空 · 水族馆里的笔记

materials.title: The aquarium notebook
materials.text:
At the aquarium, our teacher asked us to draw one fish carefully. I chose a silver fish with a dark mark near its tail. Whenever it approached the glass, I added another detail.

Soon I noticed a problem. In one sketch the mark was round; in another it looked like a line. The fish also seemed to change length. I thought I was bad at ____1____.

My friend Nia asked whether I was watching the same fish. "Of course! It has a dark mark," I said. She pointed across the tank. There were ____2____ fish with similar marks. I had drawn whichever one came closest.

A staff member showed us a white area on one fish's fin. We could recognise it from both sides. I recorded this feature as a ____3____.

Then I waited. My fish did not always swim where I wanted. Instead of ____4____ to another fish, I left parts of the drawing blank until it returned.

I also noted whether it faced me or moved sideways. Position affected the shape I ____5____, although the animal itself had not changed.

Back at school, I kept the first sketches beside the final one. I did not throw them ____6____: they recorded my discovery of the problem.

The teacher especially liked my notes. They explained ____7____ I had chosen each detail, which a neat picture alone could not show.

Now, when observing one animal, I check its ____8____ before adding a mark. The notebook helped me separate changes in the fish from changes in my ____9____. My final drawing was something I could ____10____, not just something that looked finished.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The narrator initially blames drawing skill for inconsistent sketches. They are not swimming or teaching, and the specific concern is shape rather than inability to wait.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Several similarly marked fish explain accidental switching. No contradicts their presence; invisible contradicts Nia pointing them out; wooden contradicts the live fish described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 3.
questions.explanation: The white fin feature guides identification. It is not a humorous joke, a danger warning or a title for the work.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 4.
questions.explanation: The narrator stops switching to whichever fish is near. Listening or speaking to fish does not match the visual task; returning to another fish is not the stated habit of changing targets.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Viewing direction affects the shape seen. The fish is neither bought, weighed nor touched by the observer.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Not throwing pages away preserves the record. Throw up, in and back do not express discarding the sketches in this context.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The notes give reasons for each selected detail: why. Where and when concern place/time rather than justification; whether expresses an unresolved yes/no choice rather than an explanation.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The key is identifying the same animal by its fin. Price, ownership and a personal name are not information used to recognise it in the tank.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Facing or sideways movement changes the observer's viewpoint and apparent shape. Homework, teacher and notebook do not describe that visual angle.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The notes make the evidence behind the picture explainable. A picture cannot be fed, borrowing is unrelated, and hiding it conflicts with showing sketches and notes to the teacher.
